title: Molecular Resonance Chamber
description: A chemistry lab simulation where the ShaderBall represents a volatile molecular compound suspended in a resonance chamber, and the BoomBox serves as a sonic frequency emitter used to excite the molecule. The user must calibrate frequency, amplitude, and exposure duration across multiple steps to achieve stable molecular resonance without triggering a critical overload.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a Molecular Resonance Chamber lab experiment. Load both GLB assets using GLTFLoader: place the ShaderBall at center (0,1.5,0) scaled to 1.5x as the 'molecular compound' floating and slowly rotating, and the BoomBox at (-2,0.5,1) scaled to 80x as the 'sonic frequency emitter' on a lab bench. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (4,3,5) looking at origin with OrbitControls. Use a dark lab environment with ambient light (0x334455, 0.3), a point light (0x00ccff, 2) above the ShaderBall simulating chamber glow, and a spot light (0xffffff, 1.5) on the BoomBox. Create an HTML overlay control panel with: (1) a frequency slider 20-2000 Hz, (2) an amplitude slider 0.1-10.0, (3) a waveform selector (sine/square/sawtooth), (4) an exposure duration input 1-30 seconds, (5) a 'Calibrate Emitter' button that validates frequency is 400-600 Hz range, (6) an 'Activate Pulse' button that triggers the emission sequence. When activated, animate the BoomBox with a subtle vibration using sinusoidal position offset, and emit visible particle rings (use BufferGeometry point clouds) traveling from BoomBox toward ShaderBall. The ShaderBall should glow and pulsate by dynamically adjusting emissive intensity on its materials based on amplitude value. Add a real-time status display showing: resonance percentage (0-100%), stability index, and temperature. Validate parameters: if amplitude exceeds 7.0 with frequency outside 400-600 Hz, trigger a red warning flash and 'CRITICAL OVERLOAD' message, shaking the camera. Successful resonance (frequency 440-560, amplitude 3.0-6.0, sine wave, duration 10-20s) should turn the ShaderBall emissive green and display 'STABLE RESONANCE ACHIEVED'. Track all 6+ interaction steps and log them to a visible experiment log panel on the right side.
